A paired one-sided t-test on days above 90°F (2018 vs 1948) gives a mean increase of about 2.9 days per station, with t = 2.37 and p ≈ 0.009. That is significant at the usual 5% level, so we reject the null hypothesis of no increase and conclude that the data provide strong evidence of more 90°F+ days in 2018.

When the null hypothesis is rejected, the error we could have made is a Type 1 error. That means concluding there was an increase when there really wasn't one. A Type 2 error is only possible when we fail to reject the null.

ANSWER: Type 1 Error
